items.q: What is the most common (m/c) presenting symptom of generalized slowing (decreased BMR) in primary and secondary hypothyroidism?
items.exp: Under Classical Symptoms: '1. Generalized slowing (↓ BMR) : Fatigue/tiredness (m/c)'. (Book p907)

items.q: Match the manifestations of generalized slowing in hypothyroidism — 1) Speech & Gait 2) Bowel movements 3) Neurologic reflexes 4) Body weight … A) Slow speech and slow gait B) Constipation C) Delayed deep tendon reflexes (DTR) D) Poor appetite with weight gain
items.exp: Generalized slowing affects: speech/gait (slow), bowel (constipation), reflexes (delayed DTR), and weight (poor appetite with weight gain). (Book p907)

items.q: In primary hypothyroidism, elevated TSH stimulates fibroblasts to produce matrix ___, which trap water and cause non-pitting myxedema.
items.exp: In 1° Hypothyroidism: ↑ TSH elevation -> Stimulates Fibroblast -> Stimulates Accumulation of matrix GAG's -> Traps water -> Nonpitting edema. (Book p907)

items.q: Assess the clinical consequences of matrix GAG accumulation trapping water in 1° hypothyroidism: I Facial puffiness, periorbital edema, and hoarse voice. II Macroglossia leading to obstructive sleep apnea syndrome.
opts: Both I and II are true
I is true; II is false
I is false; II is true
Both I and II are false
items.exp: Trapped water from matrix GAGs causes puffiness (face), periorbital edema, macroglossia -> obstructive sleep apnea syndrome, hoarse voice, and nonpitting edema. (Book p907)

items.q: Which of the following is NOT listed on page 907 as a symptom predominant in young females with hypothyroidism?
items.exp: Symptoms predominant in young females are hair loss, irregular menstrual cycle, dry skin, and mood swings. (Book p907)

items.q: Which endocrine disorder is noted on page 907 as causing 'False positive Hypothyroidism' (transiently elevated TSH)?
items.exp: Page 907 explicitly contains the note: 'Note : False positive Hypothyroidism -> Addison's disease'. (Book p907)

items.q: An adult with severe longstanding primary hypothyroidism presents with prominent pseudohypertrophy of both calf muscles accompanied by slowness and muscle stiffness. What eponymous disorder is depicted in the photo on page 907?
items.exp: The clinical photo on page 907 demonstrates: 'Hoffman syndrome Pseudohypertrophy in calf muscle'. (Book p907)

items.q: Match the serous cavity effusions seen in hypothyroid polyserositis — 1) Pleural cavity 2) Pericardial space 3) Peritoneal cavity … A) Pleural effusion B) Pericardial effusion C) Ascites
items.exp: Complications of hypothyroidism include serous effusions in three spaces: pleural effusion, pericardial effusion, and ascites. (Book p907)

items.q: What is the most common cause of Carpal Tunnel Syndrome (CTS) in females versus males on page 907?
items.exp: Carpal tunnel syndrome (CTS): 'm/c cause in females : Hypothyroidism' and 'm/c cause in males : Amyloidosis'. (Book p907)

items.q: Regarding Carpal Tunnel Syndrome (CTS) epidemiology on page 907: I Hypothyroidism is the most common cause in females. II Amyloidosis is the most common cause in males.
opts: Both I and II are true
I is true; II is false
I is false; II is true
Both I and II are false
items.exp: Page 907 notes for CTS: - m/c cause in females : Hypothyroidism, - m/c cause in males : Amyloidosis. (Book p907)

items.q: A 48-year-old obese woman with untreated hypothyroidism presents with severe loud snoring, daytime sleepiness, and witnessed nocturnal apneas. What anatomical mechanism links this to her thyroid disease?
opts: Macroglossia secondary to TSH-induced matrix GAG accumulation causing obstructive sleep apnea syndrome
Bilateral recurrent laryngeal nerve compression from thyroid fibrosis
Direct neuromuscular weakness of the diaphragm from hypothyroid myopathy
Tracheal deviation from subacute granulomatous expansion
items.exp: GAG accumulation traps water, producing macroglossia that leads directly to obstructive sleep apnea syndrome. (Book p907)

items.q: Although page 907 prints 'Hypocholesterolaemia' among complications (an editorial misprint in the scan), the classical metabolic consequence of reduced LDL clearance in hypothyroidism is ___.
items.exp: Page 907 lists 'Hypocholesterolemia' in its complications column, but clinically and on page 903, impaired cholesterol clearance classically causes hypercholesterolemia. (Book p907)

items.q: Which of the following is NOT listed on page 907 as a complication of hypothyroidism?
opts: Obstructive sleep apnea syndrome and Carpal tunnel syndrome
items.exp: Hypercalcemia and nephrolithiasis are complications of severe thyrotoxicosis (p903), not hypothyroidism. Complications on p907 are myxedema coma, encephalopathy, bradycardia, effusions, OSA, and CTS. (Book p907)
